literal token "RUNBOOK-OK", then propose a transition by submitting
the file path. The nitpicker reviewer will read the file and approve

runbook.sourceText:
version: 1
name: smoke-test
description: Minimal end-to-end test of the runbook machinery — one reviewer, one check, a rework path, terminal phase.
initial_phase: draft

executor:
  tools: [write, read, bash]

reviewers:
  nitpicker:
    persona: |
      You are a nitpicking reviewer. Use the `read` tool to inspect the
      submitted note file before deciding.
      Approve ONLY if ALL of these hold:
        (a) the file is non-empty,
        (b) it contains the literal token "RUNBOOK-OK",
        (c) it is fewer than 200 characters.
      Reject otherwise, giving a one-line reason in a structured finding.
    tools: [read]
    memory: { mode: fresh_with_ledger }

budgets:
  max_total_turns: 6
  max_phase_attempts: 3

phases:
  draft:
    objective: |
      Write a short note file (under 200 characters) that contains the
      literal token "RUNBOOK-OK", then propose a transition by submitting
      the file path. The nitpicker reviewer will read the file and approve
      or reject. If rejected, revise the file and propose again — this
      exercises the rework path.
    transitions:
      - to: verify
        submission:
          schema:
            type: object
            required: [file_path]
            properties:
              file_path: { type: string }
        reviews:
          - { id: nit, reviewer: nitpicker }
        decision:
          permit_when:
            eq: [{ ref: reviews.nit.verdict }, approve]

  verify:
    objective: Confirm the note file exists and is non-empty on disk.
    transitions:
      - to: done
        submission:
          schema:
            type: object
            required: [file_path]
        checks:
          - id: file-nonempty
            file_nonempty: { path_from: proposal.submission.file_path }
        decision:
          permit_when:
            eq: [{ ref: checks.file-nonempty.passed }, true]

  done:
    terminal: true
